title: The Magna Carta
examples: What did the Magna Carta actually say about rights?
How did the Magna Carta limit the king's power?
Who forced King John to sign the Magna Carta?

explain.say: The Magna Carta was signed in the year twelve fifteen.
It was signed by King John of England under pressure.
The main idea was that even the king had limits on his power.
A key concept was the rule of law for everyone in the land.

draw.text: Rule of Law: Everyone is equal

explain.say: A concrete example is that the barons demanded certain rights for themselves.
In everyday life, this idea helps us with fair court trials today.

faq.q: Why is the Magna Carta important?
faq.a: It is important because it was one of the first major documents to suggest that even a king must follow the law.
asks: What did the Magna Carta change?
Did the Magna Carta give rights to everyone?

faq.a: King John of England was forced to sign it by a group of powerful barons.
asks: Was King John happy about signing it?

faq.a: It means that no person, no matter how powerful, is above the law. Everyone must obey the established laws.
asks: Is the king above the law?
What is the rule of law?

faq.q: What was the year of the Magna Carta?
faq.a: The Magna Carta was sealed in the year twelve fifteen.
asks: When was the Magna Carta signed?
What year is the Magna Carta from?

faq.a: The barons wanted written guarantees that protected their rights and limited the king's ability to take property or raise taxes unfairly.
asks: What did the barons fight for?
What were the barons' main demands?

facts: The Magna Carta was sealed in the year twelve fifteen.
It was an agreement between King John and rebellious barons.
It established the principle that the law should be supreme.
It limited the power of the monarch in England.

quiz.say: The Magna Carta primarily established that:
quiz.show: King's power is limited by law

options.show: The barons could fight the king at any time.
options.say: The barons could fight the king at any time.

options.show: The king must follow the law.
options.say: The king must follow the law.

options.show: The king could tax people whenever he wanted.
options.say: The king could tax people whenever he wanted.

options.show: Only the nobles had any rights.
options.say: Only the nobles had any rights.

quiz.why: The document was a major step toward limiting absolute power.

wrong.0: The document was a legal agreement, not a battle plan.
wrong.2: This was the power the barons were trying to stop.
wrong.3: The goal was to create rights for more people.

quiz.say: If a king could arrest people without a trial, this would violate the idea of:
quiz.why: The rule of law means everyone, including the king, must face fair legal procedures.

wrong.0: This relates to land and service, not legal rights.
wrong.1: A royal decree is an order; the law is a rule.
wrong.3: This refers to the rights of the barons, not the general law.

quiz.say: The year twelve fifteen is significant because:

options.show: It was when King John was crowned.
options.say: It was when King John was crowned.

options.show: It was the year all English laws were rewritten.
options.say: It was the year all English laws were rewritten.

options.show: It marks the signing of the Magna Carta.
options.say: It marks the signing of the Magna Carta.

options.show: It was the year the English Civil War ended.
options.say: It was the year the English Civil War ended.

quiz.why: This specific date is when the major agreement took place.

wrong.0: The coronation happened before the conflict.
wrong.1: It was a specific agreement, not a total rewrite.
wrong.3: The Civil War happened much later in history.
